summary: babel-plugin-linaria-css-to-undefined preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a small Babel plugin that rewrites linaria css tags to undefined (lib/index.js is ~90 lines of ordinary Babel visitor code). However, package.json declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`, and setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases (bun-v1.3.13), unzips it into a temp directory, marks it executable, and then invokes that freshly downloaded Bun binary against a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB Bun-compiled, heavily obfuscated script (obfuscator.io-style rotated string arrays such as `n7gIxM`, a `WV8StW` shuffler, hex-numbered identifiers, `// @bun @bun-cjs` header) that is not referenced by the plugin's actual runtime code. Installing the package therefore fetches a second language runtime and uses it to execute a large opaque payload on the installer's host at `npm install` time, on a package whose stated Babel-plugin purpose does not require Bun or any bundled binary. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: the Bun runtime is used to run attacker-controlled bundled bytes that Node-based scanners will not introspect, and the executed payload is unrelated to the advertised functionality.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
